summary: Explains content types that break Nanite's pixel-proportional scaling (aggregate geometry like foliage, closely stacked surfaces, faceted normals) and covers Nanite foliage authoring with Preserve Area, Max WPO Displacement, static displacement mapping, runtime Nanite Tessellation setup, Nanite skeletal meshes and Nanite spline meshes.
gotchas: Nanite Tessellation and Static Displacement Mapping are experimental; r.Nanite.AllowTessellation is read-only and must be set in config
Vertex:triangle ratio of 2:1 or higher (faceted normals) makes Nanite meshes much more expensive
Masked cards and dense foliage render slower than solid geometry; enabling Nanite on card foliage is not always faster
Tessellation ignores Pixel Depth Offset, has no crack-free displacement, and large Magnitude hurts culling and VSM performance (use ~64x smaller Magnitude on Landscape)

summary: Step-by-step workflow for generating random-pose training data in Maya with the ML Deformer Data Generation plugin, importing the Alembic geometry cache and FBX, training a Neural Morph Model ML Deformer asset, and applying it to a character via the MLDeformer Component and a Deformer Graph.
gotchas: Requires the ML Deformer Framework and Neural Morph Model plugins plus an external DCC such as Maya
Training data Alembic can reach 50-100 GB; FBX and Alembic must have identical frame counts and poses
Geometry cache import must disable Flatten Tracks and enable Store Imported Vertex Numbers
Vertex Delta Model is an example only and not for production

summary: Conceptual overview of ML Cloth Simulation, which predicts cloth shape per frame from skeletal pose using an MLP low-frequency component plus a Nearest Neighbor high-frequency component trained from pre-simulated geometry caches.
gotchas: Cloth is assumed quasi-static: predicts wrinkles but not swinging or draping
Best for tight-fitting clothing, not dresses or capes

summary: Explains the Neural Network Engine (NNE) API for running neural network inference at runtime or in editor: CPU, GPU and RDG interfaces, runtime lookup, importing models as UNNEModelData assets, creating models and model instances, with a minimal C++ CPU example.
gotchas: Beta feature; use caution when shipping
Not all runtimes are available on all platforms; always check returned weak/shared pointers for validity
SetInputTensorShapes must be called before first inference and whenever input shapes change
Caller owns input/output tensor memory and must keep it valid for the whole inference call

summary: Placeholder page for the NNE quick start; it only points to an external Epic Developer Community NNE Quick Start Guide.
gotchas: Beta feature
No content in the docs; real guide is on the community portal

summary: Reference for .ini config files: section/key syntax, array operators, config categories and the load-order hierarchy, reading config into UPROPERTY(Config) or via GConfig, SaveConfig, GetIni, command-line overrides, and which sections to put console variables in.
gotchas: Command-line config overrides do not work with arrays
Config section ClassName omits the U or A prefix
Not all config settings are exposed in Project Settings
r. cvars belong in [/Script/Engine.RendererSettings]; s. in StreamingSettings; gc. in GarbageCollectionSettings

summary: How to enable and tune Dynamic Resolution, which adjusts primary screen percentage from GPU frame timings: GameUserSettings / OperationMode control, min/max screen percentage and frame budget cvars, pause/resume, stat displays, panic behaviour, platform support and replacing the heuristic in C++.
gotchas: PC support is Win64 DX12 and Vulkan only; engine blocks unsupported platforms by default
Not supported with multi-world Play-In-Editor and not in Editor viewports
Gaussian DoF and DFAO have issues with resolution changes
Post Process Volume ScreenPercentage is ignored by dynamic resolution

summary: General real-time optimization guidance: stat commands, normal map baking, reducing draw calls and material IDs, material instruction cost and translucency overdraw, texture resolution via mip debug, recommended streaming/packaging ini settings, and Size Map, Statistics and Memreport for package size and boot time.
gotchas: Console is only available in Development builds, not Shipping or Test
Draw call counts differ between PIE and on-device
Size Map shows editor footprint, typically larger than the cooked size
Uncompressed paks boot faster but increase package size

summary: Non-technical guidance on planning for scalability across artists, QA, programmers and producers: budgets, testing on a spec matrix, measuring in milliseconds, and keeping scalability settings from affecting gameplay.

Reference for the engine scalability groups and their cvars (resolution scale, view distance, anti-aliasing, post process, shadows, textures, effects, foliage), Detail Mode, Material Quality Level with the Quality Switch node, skeletal mesh LOD bias, and customizing groups via DefaultScalability.ini.
gotchas: Foliage meshes only respond to scalability if Enable Density Scaling is set
Quality Switch nodes add shader permutations and cannot be used for distance LOD
Detail Mode should only be used on objects with no gameplay effect

summary: Explains primary and secondary spatial upscaling, upscale filter quality, Temporal AA Upsample (TAAU) and its automatic view mip bias, material implications for post-process materials after upscaling, the secondary screen percentage for high-DPI, editor DPI scaling and VR pixel density.
keys: Disable DPI Based Editor Viewport Scaling
gotchas: Secondary screen percentage is static and cannot change at runtime
Automatic View Mip Bias only applies with TAAU, not TAA/MSAA/FXAA
Tonemapper merged upscale falls back if a post process material follows the tonemapper
Page predates TSR and describes TAAU-era behaviour

summary: Large table of command-line flags and -Key=Value arguments for the editor and game executables, covering RHI selection, logging, windowing/resolution, debugging (GPU crash, RDG, Vulkan validation), cooking/pak utilities, profiling and device profile overrides.
gotchas: Arguments are not case-sensitive
Many entries have no description
Some flags are deprecated (e.g. -compress, -aes, UseNSUrlConnection removed in 5.4)

summary: Overview of the legacy Material Function-based layered material workflow using Make/Break Material Attributes and MatLayerBlend functions, including a list of blend functions, how to parameterize layers via Function Inputs, and performance caveats.
gotchas: All layers are evaluated per pixel then blended, so layered materials are expensive
Prefer separate material slots over layering when per-pixel blending is not needed
Generally too heavy for mobile
Newer Material Layers feature exists as an alternative

summary: Describes the Make, Set, Break, Get and Blend Material Attributes expression nodes for bundling, splitting and blending full material attribute sets, mainly for layered materials.
gotchas: Use Material Attributes must be enabled on the material to connect attribute bundles
Set Material Attributes is preferred over Make but is not context sensitive to blend mode/shading model

summary: How to use the Material Layers system: create Material Layer and Material Layer Blend assets, add a Material Attribute Layers expression to a base material, and manage the layer stack and per-layer parameters in a Material Instance's Layer Parameters tab.
gotchas: Use Material Attributes must be enabled on the base material
The Background layer cannot be moved in the stack
A layer without a blend asset overrides layers below it

summary: Hub page for Pivot Painter, a 3ds Max MAXScript that stores pivot and rotation data in vertices for shader-driven animation; links to the 1.0 and 2.0 guides, MAXScript reference and material functions.
gotchas: Requires 3ds Max (MAXScript)

summary: Reference for Movie Render Queue job settings: Output (paths, resolution, file name tokens), Anti-Aliasing temporal/spatial samples and warm-up, Burn In, Camera shutter/overscan, Color Output OCIO, Console Variables, Debug Options, Game Overrides and High Resolution tiling.
gotchas: With TAA enabled, more than 8 total samples requires disabling AA or raising r.TemporalAASamples
Temporal Sample Count above 1 needs tracks extended a frame before the sequence start
High Resolution tiling does not support TAA, SSR, convolution bloom, lens flares
Output Frame Step is experimental; MSAA is not supported

summary: How to recognize and debug GPU crashes (TDR timeouts and page faults) on D3D12/D3D11: reading DXGI_ERROR_DEVICE_REMOVED logs, RHI breadcrumbs, DRED and NVIDIA Aftermath output, the flags and cvars that enable them, handling VRAM exhaustion, ray-tracing tiling, and raising TdrDelay in the Windows registry.
gotchas: CPU callstack of a GPU crash is irrelevant; errors are reported asynchronously
Full DRED has a significant performance cost; breadcrumbs and lightweight DRED only default on in Debug/Development
Aftermath dumps only on NVIDIA GPUs
Raising TdrDelay via registry edit is risky and won't fix all crashes; DXGI_ERROR_DEVICE_RESET usually means another app crashed
